priced_in_summary: Not TOO_LATE: the stock has FALLEN 39.50% over the trailing year on two earnings-driven drops, not risen on multiple expansion, which is the opposite of the shape method section 7 requires for that verdict. What the price does ask, on the market's own filed 9%/5-year reverse-DCF convention, is a durable FCF DECLINE (-6.49% a year) even though FY2025 delivered the company's first positive GAAP operating income in eight years and management guides FY2026 cash flow roughly flat despite a guided revenue cut concentrated in a normalizing, low-margin emergency-response line. That reads as a real, bull-favoring gap at the filed convention (+11.4 points at 5 years), but this dive's own stress-testing shows it is NOT robust: a discount rate stressed to a still-plausible 12% (given an Altman Z-score of 1.31, squarely in the distress zone) closes it, and rebasing the reverse-DCF's own free-cash-flow base to the FY2022-2025 trailing average instead of the elevated FY2025 print REVERSES the sign entirely, to an ask of +17.9% that this dive cannot defend. Combined with a live, undated strategic-review and poison-pill situation whose resolution direction is itself unknown, the honest verdict is WATCH: a real gap under the filed conventions, real enough uncertainty about those conventions and about the balance sheet to withhold a bet on it today.
bull: Segment-level disclosure attributes the FY2026 revenue cut almost entirely to a normalizing, one-time-comparison line: $37.7 million of the $47.9 million Q2 2026 YoY revenue decline traces to environmental emergency response comping "an abnormally high prior-year quarter driven by a single environmental event," not to demand loss in the core consulting/testing engine; management still guides FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA GROWTH and roughly 150 basis points of margin expansion despite the guided revenue decline, and the Measurement and Analysis segment shows "strong client demand and acceleration into the second half of 2026."

The reverse-DCF's own market-implied path prices continued FCF decline (-6.49%/yr at the filed 5-year convention, -2.90%/yr at 10 years) even though FY2025 delivered the company's first positive GAAP operating income ($11.7 million) and near-breakeven net income after seven straight years of GAAP losses, and management guides FY2026 operating cash flow "largely unchanged" ($70-80 million in H2 2026 alone) despite the revenue cut, an unusually wide gap between what the price demands and what guidance describes at only 10.56x FY2025 free cash flow.

A Board-led strategic review (announced 2026-08-05) explicitly names "evaluating acquisition interest in the Company and other value-creating transactions" among its alternatives, triggered by a disclosed "significant and undisclosed accumulation of Onterris shares and derivative securities" large enough to warrant a 15%-trigger poison pill: a live, board-sanctioned corporate-control situation on a beaten-down name that the reverse-DCF's going-concern framing prices nowhere.
bear: FY2026 revenue guidance was cut to $740.0-790.0 million from $840.0-900.0 million at the same release that disclosed the poison pill, roughly a 12% guide-down at the midpoint one quarter after the company was still guiding UP off a record FY2025; the stock fell 33.32% in the single session around that print (2026-08-05 close $22.63 to 2026-08-06 close $15.09), and a management team defending against an activist during a live strategic review has every incentive to frame a genuine deceleration as one-off.

Altman Z-score is 1.31, squarely in the DISTRESS zone (below the conventional 1.8 cutoff), against net_debt/EBITDA of 5.19x on a GAAP-EBITDA basis, and the accumulated deficit WIDENED from -$273.5 million (2025-12-31) to -$284.8 million (2026-06-30) in a quarter the company reported a GAAP profit, driven by $30.0 million of share buybacks and $10.8 million of contingent-consideration payments funded while H1 2026 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE $5.5 million (against +$27.4 million in H1 2025).

The reverse-DCF's own $91.159 million free-cash-flow base is 2.81x the FY2022-2025 four-year average of $32.393 million, the same base-year-outlier pattern this analyst's own log has now flagged on four of six prior dives (MYRG 2.90x, 688425.SS 2.00x, ESLT 2.65x); stress-tested here rather than merely declared, rebasing to that trailing average does not make the bull case easier to defend, it REVERSES it, raising the market's implied ask from -6.49% to +17.90% at the same 5-year convention, an ask this dive's own 4.93% build cannot clear.

rows.why: A crude FY2025 return on invested capital, computed here and not disclosed, is essentially zero: net income -$843,000 over invested capital of $728.240 million (long-term debt $277.065 million plus equity $451.175 million), about -0.12%. Net income is used as the NOPAT proxy deliberately, so no tax rate is assumed. This dive defends a modest recovery to roughly 3.5% by FY2030 under the same revenue and margin path as the two rows above (FY2030 operating income of roughly $48.3 million at 5.0% margin on $966.2 million revenue, less an estimated $22.75 million of net interest expense on the current $325.05 million net-debt base at a 7% average rate, against a roughly flat invested-capital base since guided deleveraging funds buybacks rather than net debt paydown). Even this recovery sits below the 9% discount rate the market's own reverse-DCF assumes as a cost of capital, which is itself a bear-leaning finding named plainly here rather than smoothed into the bull case: on this dive's own numbers, Onterris is not yet earning its cost of capital even in the improving scenario.

No disagreement, and saying so is worth a row. 2.5% perpetual growth is a reasonable long-run nominal assumption for a US environmental-services consultancy with a structural regulatory tailwind, and this dive would not move it. The assumption this dive actually questions is the DISCOUNT RATE (9%): given an Altman Z-score of 1.31 (distress zone) and 5.19x net-debt-to-EBITDA on a GAAP basis, 9% may understate the return a rational buyer would require. Method section 7 forbids re-solving the filed column in session; the discount-rate stress is disclosed separately in net_gap_direction and bear[1], not as a replacement for the filed number.

rows.note: Built like for like rather than compared revenue against FCF. Revenue $830.538 million growing to $966.097 million in FY2030 at the 3.07% path defended in row 1, at a 12% forward FCF margin (a modest step up from FY2025's own elevated 10.98%, consistent with the guided margin expansion in the operating_margin row) gives FY2030 free cash flow of $115.932 million, a 4.93% FCF CAGR from the $91.159 million FY2025 base. Against the filed 5-year market-implied -6.49%, the gap is +11.42 percentage points, well outside this file's own 3.59-point horizon_spread: a real gap by the file's own rule, in the BULLISH direction (the opposite polarity from every prior dive in this log, where the market always asked for MORE than the dive could defend). Against the filed 10-year market-implied -2.90%, the same build is +7.83 points ahead, still outside the horizon_spread: the sign does not flip between horizons, only the size narrows, consistent with the shorter explicit period always demanding the more extreme (here, more negative) annual rate for the same enterprise value. STRESS-TESTED, not just declared, on the two inputs this analyst's log has learned to distrust most: (1) DISCOUNT RATE. Reproducing quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection formula exactly (verified to reproduce the filed 5/7/10-year readings, -0.06493/-0.04439/-0.02896 against the filed -0.0649/-0.0444/-0.029, before varying anything) and raising the discount rate from the filed 9% shows the implied ask rising (becoming less negative, then positive) as the rate rises: -4.94% at 9.5%, -3.45% at 10%, -0.65% at 11%, +1.97% at 12%. At 12% -- not an unreasonable rate for a name with an Altman Z-score of 1.31 -- the gap against this dive's 4.93% build narrows to +2.96 points, INSIDE the 3.59-point horizon_spread: not a measurable gap at all by the file's own rule. (2) BASE YEAR. The filed base_fcf ($91.159 million) is 2.81x the FY2022-2025 four-year average ($32.393 million), the same base-year-outlier defect class this log has now flagged five times. Unlike MYRG and 688425.SS, where rebasing to the trailing average made the market's ask EASIER to clear (the same direction ESLT's stress found), rebasing here at the filed 9% rate RAISES the ask to +17.90% at 5 years and +10.88% at 10 years, ABOVE this dive's own 4.93% build in both cases: on that base, the gap flips NEGATIVE (roughly -13 points), the market asking for MORE than this dive can defend, the same polarity as every other dive in this log. The finding therefore survives only if BOTH the filed 9% discount rate AND the elevated FY2025 base year are the right conventions to trust, and this dive cannot independently confirm either; see independence_test.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: At the filed 9%-discount-rate, 5-year, FY2025-base convention, the reverse-DCF's own solve asks for free cash flow to CONTRACT at -6.49% a year for five years; this dive's own like-for-like build (3.07% revenue CAGR off the FY2026-guided trough, GAAP operating margin recovering from FY2025's 1.41% toward roughly 5.0% by FY2030, a 12% forward FCF margin) implies FCF GROWING at roughly +4.93% a year, an 11.42-percentage-point gap in the bullish direction, on a name trading at 10.56x FY2025 free cash flow that just delivered its first positive GAAP operating income in eight fiscal years.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: The category of market error this dive names is a single volatile comparison line (environmental emergency response, a disaster-response revenue category the company's own segment disclosure says swung from an abnormally high comparison quarter to a historically low one) being extrapolated into a structural growth-rate decline, compounded by a governance-uncertainty discount: an undisclosed party has accumulated 15%-plus of the company's shares and derivatives, triggering a poison pill and a board-led strategic review with no set timetable, the kind of overhang that depresses a multiple independent of the cash-flow path itself. This dive's own stress-testing shows the finding is NOT robust to every convention, though: it survives the 10-year horizon and a discount rate stressed as high as roughly 11%, but a 12% discount rate (not unreasonable given the Altman Z-score of 1.31, squarely in the distress zone) closes it, and rebasing the reverse-DCF's own free-cash-flow base to the FY2022-2025 trailing average instead of the elevated FY2025 print REVERSES the sign entirely, to an ask of +17.90% this dive cannot defend. So the market error this dive claims is real only if the filed 9% discount rate and the elevated FY2025 base year are both the right conventions, and this dive cannot independently confirm that either is, which is why the verdict below stays at WATCH rather than INVESTABLE.
independence_test.falsification: Q3 2026 results (expected early-to-mid November 2026, inside review_by, on the company's Aug-5 quarterly cadence) reporting revenue within or above the guided $190.0-210.0 million range AND Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin at or above the guided 17.0%-18.0% (against Q2 2026's 17.1%) would confirm the 'one-time comparison, not structural decline' read behind the revenue_cagr_5y and operating_margin rows; a second consecutive quarter of Adjusted EBITDA margin below 17.0%, or a further full-year revenue or EBITDA guide-down at that same release, would falsify it and support the market's own decline-priced-in read instead.

earnings_quality.basis: None of grade C's three named triggers are actually present: Beneish is CLEAN (-3.049 against the -1.78 review threshold, 12 of 12 inputs), DSO shows no sustained drift (65.80 / 63.49 / 65.71 / 83.26 / 68.28 days, FY2021-FY2025: it spiked in FY2024 and REVERTED in FY2025, the opposite of a sustained trend), and the balance sheet carries no deferred-revenue or contract-liability line at all to drift (Onterris bills on a contract-ASSET, percentage-of-completion basis, the opposite structure from a subscription or milestone-billing business). Two mild flags with defensible explanations put this at grade B rather than A: (1) capex-to-depreciation ran below 1.0x every year FY2022-2025 (0.20x / 0.65x / 0.40x / 0.32x), a mechanical underinvestment signal, defensible because Onterris runs an asset-light professional-services model and carries growing finance-lease right-of-use assets ($36.630 million at 2026-06-30) consistent with financing equipment via leases rather than capex, and PP&E net has still RISEN over the period ($36.045 million FY2022 to $63.853 million FY2025) despite the low ratio; (2) contract assets (unbilled revenue) grew from $58.831 million (2025-12-31) to $66.293 million (2026-06-30), +12.68% over two quarters, faster than revenue over the same window, a mild revenue-recognition-timing watch item defensible as ordinary percentage-of-completion timing on the Assessment/Permitting/Response engineering projects this dive's placement rests on. The accrual ratio (NI minus CFO, over average total assets) is -10.99% in FY2025 and -9.36% in FY2024, both LARGER in magnitude than the 5% grade-A caution band, but in the FAVORABLE direction (cash earnings exceed net income in both years) and mechanically distorted by a near-zero net-income denominator (FY2025 net income was -$843,000 against $107.476 million of operating cash flow); the same distortion the O1 profile's own quality block names for operating_cash_flow_to_net_income. Not treated as a manipulation flag, but also not counted toward grade A's clean bar given the magnitude. SEPARATELY, and NOT itself an earnings-quality veto input under method section 7's four named checks: Altman Z-score is 1.31, squarely in the DISTRESS zone (8 of 8 inputs found), against net_debt/EBITDA of 5.19x on a GAAP-EBITDA basis and an accumulated deficit that widened $11.324 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-06-30 even in a GAAP-profitable quarter. This is a genuine balance-sheet-fragility caution, distinct from the manipulation question the A-D grade answers, and is carried forward into bear[1] and the independence test rather than folded into or diluting this grade.

inputs.deferred_revenue_drift_basis: No deferred-revenue or contract-liability line exists on Onterris' balance sheet (data/edgar/docs/ONT.json 8-K EX-99.1 condensed balance sheet, 2026-06-30 and 2025-12-31 columns, verified verbatim): current liabilities list accounts payable, accrued payroll, contingent consideration, lease and debt lines only, no 'deferred revenue' or 'contract liabilities' caption. Instead the ASSET side carries Contract assets (unbilled revenue), $66.293 million (2026-06-30) vs $58.831 million (2025-12-31), +12.68%, the opposite balance-sheet structure from a company that bills in advance; recorded as the second mild flag above rather than forced into a 'drift' framing that does not apply to this issuer's revenue-recognition model.

would_buy_zone.basis: The band at which this dive's own defended FCF-CAGR-equivalent build (3.08%-4.93%, depending on whether forward FCF margin holds at FY2025's own elevated 10.98% or expands to a guided-consistent 12% by FY2030) would clear the reverse-DCF's own ask WITHOUT relying on the elevated FY2025 base year net_gap_direction and bear[2] flag as 2.81x the FY2022-2025 trailing average. Rebasing quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection formula (9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth, 5-year explicit period; replication verified to reproduce the filed 5/7/10-year readings to 4 decimal places before varying anything) to the $32.393 million trailing-average free-cash-flow base and forward-solving for the price at which the resulting ask falls to this dive's own build gives $5.53 (conservative, flat-10.98%-margin build) to $6.73 (guided-margin-expansion build, 4.93% FCF CAGR), both converted to price via the same net-debt bridge the filed solve implies ($325.05 million net debt over 35,929,665 shares). At today's $17.74, the FILED convention's own elevated base already looks cheap against this dive's build (the ask does not rise to 4.93% until $35.36, above spot); this zone deliberately prices the harsher, trailing-average-base convention instead, because this dive cannot independently confirm which base year is the right one to trust (see independence_test and bear[2]), and a zone drawn on the convention that already favors the thesis would not be a real margin of safety. Both bounds sit within 0.3x-2.0x of the last close ($5.32-$35.48).
